Key facts recorded from the pinned tree:

- The only credentials in `tomcat-tribes` are the Kubernetes service-account token (`TokenStreamProvider.java:57-58`) and the client key (`CertificateStreamProvider.java:59-83`), so CWE-311 maps onto the cloud membership TLS path.
- A/B asymmetry on the same method: token branch defaults to `https` (`KubernetesMembershipProvider.java:85-87`), client-certificate branch defaults to `http` (`:101-103`); the URL is then built from that value (`:128-133`) and opened by a shared opener that only applies the configured socket factory when the connection is an `HttpsURLConnection` (`AbstractStreamProvider.java:112-122`).
- The TLS trust setup has a second, trust-all implementation (`AbstractStreamProvider.java:49-62`, `:153-156`; `InsecureStreamProvider.java:22-34`), currently unreachable from the shipped provider because a CA path is always supplied (`KubernetesMembershipProvider.java:80-82`).
- Encryption gaps in the channel layer: `EncryptInterceptor` replaces only `ChannelData.getMessage()` (`EncryptInterceptor.java:110-121`) while the package header and sender `Member` stay clear (`ChannelData.java:178-196`); membership heartbeats bypass the chain (`McastServiceImpl.java:504-523`); `TcpFailureDetector` writes a package straight to a socket (`TcpFailureDetector.java:359-377`) under a guard that only checks ordering (`EncryptInterceptor.java:86-95`); `decrypt` has no short-message check although its localized key exists unused (`LocalStrings.properties:24`).

Verdict: usable, with 7 independent groups; recommended stack is T1+T2 (M5/M3), T3 (M2), T4 (M4), T6 (M1). The A/B site identification is inferred from code asymmetry — the fix commits themselves were not readable from the worktree, and that is flagged in `unverified`.
